{{Quote|We'll leave as soon as you're ready. Docking Bay Ninety-four.|Han Solo, to Obi-Wan Kenobi and Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
'''Docking Bay 94''' (also known as '''Hangar 94'''), one of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley's]] 362 [[Hangar/Legends|docking bays]] scattered throughout the [[City/Legends|city]], was where the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] waited to rendezvous with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and where a notorious meeting between [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] took place about a [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[The Hutt Gambit|shipment tragedy]] Solo had never paid back. Aside from the ''Millennium Falcon'' itself, the hangar also contained at least three repulsorlift shuttles.<ref name="SW1991">[[Star Wars (1991 video game)|''Star Wars'' video game (1991)]]</ref>

[[Ohwun De Maal/Legends|Ohwun De Maal]] and his [[Chachi De Maal/Legends|wife]] owned this bay along with five others nearby. The docking bay was owned by Ohwun's father and his grandfather before him.<ref name="GG7">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref>

Docking Bay 94, like all of the bays in Mos Eisley, consisted of an entrance ramp and a restraining wall that surrounded a shallow pit. The pit absorbed and deflected the blasts made when [[Starship/Legends|starships]] landed or took off. By law, ships with [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]] were required to use them when entering and leaving the docking bays.

The docking bay cost 25 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] per day to use. A resupply and restocking service cost 8 credits. Replacement [[Fuel cell/Legends|fuel cells]] cost 10 credits.<ref name="GG7" />

==History==
The docking bay became the scene of a firefight between Han Solo and a squad of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] led by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Mod Terrik]], having been informed about the location of the droids by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Spy/Legends|spymaster]] [[Garindan/Legends|Garindan]], as the former attempted to escape Tatooine with his passengers.

Shortly before he was forced to flee [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], Han Solo was confronted by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] and his gang in Docking Bay 94 over Solo's debt to Jabba and the recent killing of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]]. Solo managed to sweet-talk Jabba with the promise of a percentage of his next job and Jabba and his gang left.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Docking_Bay_94_SWI95.png|thumb|left|250px|The number 94 printed on the wall]]

After filming had finished on the set of Docking Bay 94 the set was transformed into the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] [[Docking Bay 327/Legends|Docking Bay 327]], since the set of the ''Millennium Falcon'' did not fit out the stage doors.

The scene in which Han Solo and Jabba have a showdown over an unpaid debt went through numerous changes between the original release and the Special Edition; originally, the actor [[Declan Mulholland]] portrayed Jabba. [[George Lucas]] stated in the DVD commentary that he intended to replace Mulholland with a stop-motion puppet effect but as the budget and schedule were running well over what was expected the filmed scenes were shelved. Later, in [[1997]], digital technology allowed [[Lucasfilm]] to use a computer-generated imagery for Jabba the Hutt more in line as he appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']]. The Special Edition version is canonical.

The number 94 appears on the walls of the docking bay.<ref name="Star Wars Insider 95">{{InsiderCite|95|May The Facts Be With You: Part Two|May The Facts Be With You: Part Two: #51-100}}</ref>

After killing Greedo, Han Solo went to Docking Bay 94. There, while Solo was talking to Jabba, it appeared that Greedo was shown in the background. However, it was a different [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] working for Jabba. In fact, Jabba had three Rodians in his party, all similarly dressed.
